clue.text: Zulus find officer carrying murdered brother.

indicators.note: an officer carrying something holds it within, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a mate is a ship's officer
Abel was the brother murdered by Cain in Genesis

explanation.surface: Someone discovers an officer bearing the body of a slain brother among Zulu warriors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' is the container signal. The Matabele (Ndebele) of Zimbabwe are a people of Zulu origin.
explanation.definitionFit: The Matabele are a southern African people descended from a Zulu offshoot, so the setter treats them as Zulus.

clue.text: Slave of Islam Emma converted to saint

indicators.note: converted means changed in form, so the letters of Emma are rearranged

parts.note: St Luke the evangelist

explanation.surface: A woman named Emma changed her faith and became a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' rearranges EMMA into MAME, and the religious surface hides the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mamelukes were a caste of slave soldiers who came to rule Egypt.

clue.text: Hill dwellers lit up with a herb.

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill
men are dwellers

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word lit is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Hill folk light up a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LIT into TIL. A tor is a rocky hill on Dartmoor.
explanation.definitionFit: Tormentil is a yellow-flowered plant of the rose family used as an astringent.

clue.text: Many in the city set.?

indicators.note: in places the letter for many inside the city's name

parts.note: Bath is a spa city in Somerset, England
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a lot

explanation.surface: Lots of people in town are settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts C inside BATH. Many standing for C (100) is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A batch is a group or set of things made together.

clue.text: Hates. hotels — a peculiar sort

indicators.note: a peculiar sort is an odd arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone detests hotels of a strange kind.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe is to detest strongly.

clue.text: Rigorous but honest in speech

indicators.note: in speech tells us the word for honest is to be heard spoken, not read

parts.note: an honest person is straight

explanation.surface: Someone is strict yet sincere whenever they talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Strait in its old sense means strict or narrow, as in 'strait is the gate'.

clue.text: Staff liable to strike ?

parts.note: not workers going on strike but a policeman's club used to hit

explanation.definitionFit: A truncheon is a short stick or baton carried by police to hit with.

clue.text: Useful quality for lift-girl, in short

annotationWithheld.why: Useful quality for lift-girl, in short (5): the def is 'Useful quality' but no parse of 'for lift-girl, in short' building ASSET could be found or confirmed
annotationWithheld.clue: Useful quality for lift-girl, in short

clue.text: Irritable, and so on, in your old 'form …

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for and so on inside the old possessive

parts.note: thy is the archaic form of your
etc is short for et cetera, and so on

explanation.surface: Short-tempered, and so forth, in your old manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'your old form' points to the archaic possessive, not a school form.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetchy means peevish or short-tempered.

clue.text: … and quick to be irritable here?

explanation.definitionFit: Snappy means both brisk and short-tempered.

clue.text: Writer gets foreign money I want collected

parts.note: the mark was the German currency

indicators.note: collected means gathered and put together anew, so the letters of 'I want' are rearranged

explanation.surface: An author receives foreign currency that someone wishes gathered in.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain, author of Huckleberry Finn, is a famous American writer.

clue.text: Disturbing sort of price?

definitions.meaning: an ... price is the reserve price at which an auction lot is offered

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means troubled or troubling; at auction the minimum starting figure is called the upset price.

clue.text: That blood sucking artist!.

definitions.meaning: a worm that sucks blood, used by old doctors
John ... was the Victorian Punch cartoonist who illustrated Dickens

explanation.definitionFit: The bloodsucking worm shares its name with John Leech, the Victorian cartoonist and illustrator.

clue.text: Bound to meet people in this game

parts.note: to bound is to hop or leap
the Scotch is an old name for the Scottish people

explanation.surface: Leaping to greet others is the essence of this pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopscotch is a children's playground game of hopping through chalked squares.

clue.text: Marlowe has numbers of little pets

parts.note: the playwright Christopher Marlowe was known as Kit
tens are numbers

explanation.surface: The Elizabethan playwright keeps several small pets.
explanation.walkthrough: The playwright Christopher Marlowe was commonly called Kit Marlowe.
explanation.definitionFit: Young cats are popular small household pets.

clue.text: Merchants who started as railway staff ?.

parts.note: ex means former, describing those who started out as something else
porters carry luggage at railway stations

explanation.surface: Traders who began their careers carrying bags on the railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Exporters are merchants who sell goods abroad.

clue.text: Gives up and returns

definitions.meaning: to give up is to surrender or concede
returns are the profits an investment produces

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is surrendering; the other is the income an investment produces.

clue.text: Reward, put up possibly rests' with judges

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the word is set upwards, read bottom to top

parts.note: meed is an old word for reward

indicators.note: possibly signals another arrangement of the letters of rests

explanation.surface: A prize is raised, and perhaps it lies with the magistrates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns MEED into DEEM; 'possibly' rearranges RESTS into STERS. Deemsters are the judges of the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Deemsters are the two justices of the Isle of Man.

clue.text: Ascetics top the personal columns.

parts.note: not newspaper notices but hermits who each lived atop a pillar of their own

explanation.definitionFit: Stylites were early Christian hermits who lived on top of pillars.

clue.text: Inclined to 'take work in northern transport ?

indicators.note: in places the word for work inside the vehicle

parts.note: a sled is transport for the snowy north
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone is minded to bring their work aboard a vehicle in the far north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'Inclined' looks like 'disposed' but here means slanting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inclined is tilted at an angle, like a slope.

clue.text: River club enters : controversy.

indicators.note: enters means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
a bat is a club

explanation.surface: A rowing club on the river joins an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enters' is the container signal; 'club' suggests a society on the river, but it is a cricket bat.
explanation.definitionFit: A debate is a formal argument or dispute.

clue.text: Study what's written in this setting

parts.note: to con is an old verb for to study
a text is what is written

explanation.surface: Examine the written words of this particular passage.
explanation.definitionFit: Context is the surrounding background or circumstances of something.

clue.text: S. 12-a different part of London

indicators.note: different means made otherwise, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 12 across, a bloodsucker

explanation.surface: A clue cross-references another to name a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges S, the answer to 12 across, and A. Chelsea is a district of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Chelsea is a fashionable district in west London.

clue.text: Flowers 'might be preferred ?

definitions.meaning: preferred shares are one kind on the stock market

explanation.definitionFit: These are scented garden blooms, and also shares, which can be preference shares.

clue.text: Good 'enough retreat in island-get about a good deal

indicators.note: retreat means go backwards, so the whole run of pieces is read back to front

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile
re means about or concerning
a lot means a good deal

explanation.surface: An acceptable withdrawal to an island earns a fair amount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' turns the whole run ELBA + RE + LOT backwards, giving TOL ER ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tolerable is acceptable or passable.

clue.text: Girl learner has a spiritualistic air

parts.note: L is the learner sign on a car
an aura is the subtle glow or atmosphere spiritualists perceive

explanation.surface: A young woman learning has an otherworldly air.
explanation.definitionFit: Laura is a girl's name.

clue.text: A growing boy'?

parts.note: a herb that grows in the garden which is also a boy's name

explanation.definitionFit: Basil is a garden herb, something grown, and also a boy's name.

clue.text: The thicket may stop us

definitions.meaning: a clump of dense brushwood or bracken
a device on a vehicle that halts it

explanation.definitionFit: A brake is a tangle of undergrowth, and also the device that slows a vehicle.

clue.text: Reason, for action

definitions.meaning: a reason or motive behind something
a legal action or lawsuit is a ... in law

explanation.definitionFit: A cause is a motive, and in law it is a suit brought before a court.

clue.text: Will try to come by morning, ten roughly'

parts.note: to try is to test

indicators.note: roughly means imprecisely arranged, so the letters of ten are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone will attempt to arrive in the morning, around ten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' rearranges TEN to ENT. 'Will' looks like a verb but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A last will and testament is the legal document disposing of one's estate.

clue.text: Scanty supply of boxes with key

parts.note: to box is to spar, so boxes are spars
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A meagre stock of packing cases comes with a single key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxes' is the verb: one who boxes spars.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse means thinly scattered or meagre.

clue.text: Touching. expressions of affection

parts.note: fond gestures made by stroking, with touching meaning both moving and physical contact

explanation.definitionFit: Caresses are gentle strokes, physical tokens of fondness.
